job.title: Principal Electrical Engineer
job.description:
Want to be a part of Asia Pacific & Middle East's (APME) largest, most innovative, and rapidly growing data centre company?

AirTrunk is a hyperscale data centre company with a powerful purpose - to scale and sustain the relentless growth of the region’s digital future. We do this by continuously redefining and delivering the digital infrastructure that meet the needs of our customers - the world’s most transformational companies. And we’re doing so sustainably, for today and tomorrow.

Having opened Australia’s first and largest hyperscale data centres in 2017, we set our eyes on rapid expansion and now operate a platform of hyperscale data centres across the APME region. With backing from our investors, including Blackstone, this is just the beginning…

Come join the A-Team at AirTrunk, where the cloud meets the ground.

A Snapshot

As Principal Electrical Engineer, you will report to the Senior Director, Engineering and be based at our North Sydney headquarters. You will lead AirTrunk's electrical engineering discipline and its team of electrical Subject Matter Experts (SMEs), working across Design and Engineering, Development, Procurement, Construction and Commissioning. You will make an impact in the following ways:

  • Lead, develop and empower a high-performing team of electrical engineering SMEs, setting clear accountabilities, strengthening technical capability and building succession coverage.
  • Act as AirTrunk's senior electrical technical authority, escalation point and delegated decision maker for material electrical risks, interpretations and design decisions.
  • Own the lifecycle of global electrical engineering and construction standards and electrical Owner-Supplied Equipment (OSE) specifications, ensuring they remain current, practical, controlled and consistently adopted.
  • Forecast and allocate electrical engineering resources across the global project pipeline according to project risk, design maturity and business priority, balancing workload and continuity.
  • Provide risk-based technical direction and independent design assurance from concept through IFC, confirming compliance with AirTrunk standards without owning day-to-day project design coordination or driving the general contractor's design development.
  • Be accountable for the discipline's cost outcomes, technical compliance and engineering suitability, including safety, resilience, operability, constructability, maintainability and lifecycle value.
  • Drive global consistency, standardisation and value engineering while protecting safety, regulatory compliance, resilience, customer commitments and operational performance.
  • Turn lessons from design, delivery, commissioning and operations into improvements to standards, specifications, assurance practices and team capability.

Your Day to Day

  • Lead the electrical SME team through clear objectives, coaching, performance management, development planning, recruitment and succession management.
  • Maintain a forward electrical resource plan and assign appropriately skilled SMEs to projects and technical initiatives, resolving priority or capacity conflicts with the Senior Director, Engineering.
  • Set electrical technical direction and acceptance criteria across LV distribution systems, standby generation, UPS systems, BESS systems earthing, protection and grading, power quality, controls interfaces and electrical OSE.
  • Establish the scope, timing and depth of risk-based electrical reviews across concept, preliminary, schematic, detailed and IFC design stages, and verify that agreed actions are closed.
  • Review designs and technical submissions to confirm alignment with AirTrunk standards, approved project requirements, applicable codes and customer commitments. Design Management retains ownership of project design coordination and the project design basis, while project delivery teams and their designers remain responsible for developing the design.
  • Serve as the senior electrical escalation point and make timely, evidence-based decisions within delegated authority; clearly record the decision, rationale, risks, conditions and accountable owner.
  • Approve, reject or escalate electrical departures, waivers, interpretations, substitutions and material non-conformances in accordance with the technical authority framework and risk appetite.
  • Own and approve electrical engineering and construction standards and OSE specifications, including review cadence, change control, stakeholder consultation, release communication, implementation guidance and evidence of adoption.
  • Maintain visibility of electrical cost drivers and benchmarks, challenge unnecessary complexity and sponsor value engineering that improves capital efficiency, programme, repeatability, energy performance or lifecycle cost without weakening technical outcomes.
  • Assess the suitability of electrical designs and equipment for safety, compliance, reliability, resilience, efficiency, constructability, maintainability, operability, scalability and intended service life.
  • Partner with Procurement and Supply Chain to evaluate vendor proposals, technical deviations, equipment substitutions and quality risks, and provide senior technical input to factory acceptance testing and proof-of-concept activities.
  • Lead discipline peer reviews and resolve interfaces with mechanical, controls and automation, civil, structural, architectural, fire and commissioning teams; maintain effective alignment with the HV delivery team.
  • Champion Safety in Design and ensure material electrical hazards, assumptions, constraints and residual risks are identified, treated and communicated to the appropriate owner.
  • Provide senior technical support for significant site, commissioning and operational issues, then ensure root causes and lessons learned are reflected in standards, specifications and future project assurance.
  • Communicate complex electrical matters clearly to executives, customers, commercial teams, delivery partners and non-technical stakeholders, including recommended options and trade-offs.

Measures of Success

  • A capable, engaged electrical SME team with clear accountabilities, strong retention, effective succession coverage and demonstrable technical development.
  • Projects resourced in line with risk, design maturity and agreed priorities, with electrical reviews and technical actions completed to required stage-gate timeframes.
  • Electrical standards and OSE specifications reviewed to the approved cadence, consistently adopted across regions and improved using documented delivery and operational learning.
  • Electrical cost outcomes supported by transparent benchmarks, disciplined scope decisions and value engineering that preserves required performance and compliance.
  • Improved first-time-right design quality, with fewer repeated deviations, late changes, design-related RFIs, non-conformances and commissioning defects.
  • Material electrical risks, departures and decisions resolved or escalated promptly, with clear accountability and auditable records.
  • Electrical systems and equipment demonstrably suitable for their intended application across safety, resilience, operability, maintainability, constructability and lifecycle value.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a closely related discipline; a relevant postgraduate qualification is advantageous.
  • Typically 12+ years of progressive electrical engineering experience, including leadership of senior engineers or SMEs across complex, multi-project or multi-region portfolios.
  • Chartered or Professional Engineer status, or an equivalent recognized registration, is preferred.
  • Deep expertise in mission-critical electrical systems, including HV and LV distribution, generation, UPS, earthing, protection and grading, power quality and electrical controls interfaces.
  • Strong experience in data centres, mission-critical facilities, industrial infrastructure or another high-availability operating environment.
  • Demonstrated experience owning engineering standards or equipment specifications and applying technical assurance, delegated authority, configuration control and deviation governance.
  • Proven ability to plan and deploy specialist resources across competing projects while maintaining quality, responsiveness and global consistency.
  • Commercially astute, with experience evaluating discipline cost, value engineering, vendor proposals, lifecycle cost and technical trade-offs.
  • A decisive and accountable leader who can resolve ambiguity, challenge constructively and communicate complex technical matters to diverse stakeholders.
  • Willingness to travel occasionally across AirTrunk's regions to support critical reviews, technical issues and team engagement.

The AirTrunk Culture

Working at AirTrunk is a once in a lifetime opportunity to fast-track your career and amplify your impact. Whilst you’re helping scale our region’s digital future, we’ll help you Grow@Hyperscale and unleash your full potential.

The pace in which we operate means you’ll feel an electric atmosphere at AirTrunk. We are a team of challengers and collaborative problem solvers who break new ground every day. We do this by living our values, going above and beyond, and being dynamic, transparent, and responsive.

Every AirTrunker brings their own unique background and diverse perspective to find solutions to problems that matter. We make sure you have everything you need to make your mark and thrive in a flexible and safe working environment, where everyone feels welcome. Our benefits empower AirTrunkers to stay positively charged.

Now’s your chance to [Grow@Hyperscale](mailto:Grow@Hyperscale).

To all recruitment agencies: AirTrunk does not accept agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to our jobs alias, AirTrunk employees or any other organisation location. AirTrunk is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

job.title: Critical Facilities Engineer (HVAC) - Melbourne, Victoria, Australia
job.description:

job.title: Executive Secretary, Corporate Office
job.description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

The Executive Secretary provides high-level, strategic secretarial and administrative support to the Corporate Office, enabling the effective management of executive priorities, stakeholder engagements, and organisational governance. The role requires exceptional discretion, executive maturity, and the ability to operate within a complex, fast-paced, and matrix environment while supporting enterprise-level decision-making.

Key Responsibilities

1. Executive Office & Strategic Support

  • Provide comprehensive and proactive secretarial support to the Corporate Office, including managing a highly complex and dynamic calendar.
  • Anticipate priorities and align schedules to support strategic objectives and critical business decisions.
  • Prepare, review, and quality-check correspondence, presentations, board papers, and executive briefings to the highest standard.
  • Act as a trusted gatekeeper to the Corporate office, exercising sound judgment in prioritising requests and managing access.
  • Handle highly sensitive and confidential matters with professionalism, integrity, and discretion.

2. Stakeholder & Communication Management

  • Serve as a key liaison between the Corporate office and internal/external stakeholders, including senior management, board members, regulators, partners, and clients.
  • Facilitate clear and efficient communication flow between the Corporate office and business units.
  • Manage and coordinate high-level engagements, including leadership meetings, town halls, and external events.

4. Office & Priority Management

  • Monitor deadlines, key deliverables, and commitments arising from executive meetings and correspondence.
  • Ensure timely follow-up and coordination across multiple stakeholders to drive execution.
  • Identify and implement improvements to administrative processes to enhance efficiency and effectiveness.

5. Travel & Engagement Planning

  • Coordinate complex international and local travel arrangements, including itineraries, logistics, and briefing materials.
  • Support preparation for external engagements, conferences, and key organisational events.

6. Project & Ad-hoc Support

  • Provide administrative and coordination support for CEO-led strategic initiatives and cross-functional projects.
  • Assist in preparing executive communications, presentations, and corporate announcements.

Key Requirements & Qualifications

  • Diploma or Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Management, or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 8–10 years’ experience in a senior executive secretary or executive assistant role, preferably supporting CEO/C-suite leadership.
  • Experience supporting board-level administration and governance processes is highly preferred.
  • Strong organisational, planning, and time-management skills with meticulous attention to detail.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • High level of integrity, confidentiality, and professionalism.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and collaboration tools.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities independently in a fast-paced environment.

Key Competencies

  • Executive maturity and presence
  • Strong judgment and confidentiality
  • Stakeholder and relationship management
  • High accountability and follow-through
  • Ability to navigate complex, multi-stakeholder environments
  • Proactive and solution-oriented mindset

job.title: Mechanical Procurement Manager
job.description:
• Lead the mechanical procurement function within the CDC Data Centres team! Manage a small, high-performing team of specialists
  • Drive supplier strategy, contract negotiations, and procurement outcomes across major capital projects across AU + NZ
  • Role to be based across our Melbourne CBD office, and Western Suburbs campuses (Brooklyn + Laverton)

About Us

Established in 2007, CDC Data Centres is Australia and New Zealand’s leading operator of secure, world-class data centre facilities. CDC plays a unique role in the fabric of the nations in which we operate, and we take this responsibility very seriously.

With multiple facilities across Australia and New Zealand, CDC’s diversified operations provide large-scale secure data centre campuses that support co-location, dedicated and hyperscale compute environments, with all campuses interconnected with high-speed carrier grade networks.

At CDC, we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity. We believe that everyone’s unique experiences enable us to deliver meaningful benefits for our people, our clients and communities. Our mission is to attract, retain and grow the world’s best data centre team.

Our people are committed, tenacious and meticulous in supporting our customers. Together, we configure the landscape to meet the security, reliability, connectivity and sustainability needs for today and tomorrow.

About the Role

As the Mechanical Procurement Manager, you will lead the procurement and commercial management of critical mechanical infrastructure supporting CDC's industry-leading data centre developments across Australia and New Zealand. You will be responsible for driving procurement strategies, managing key supplier and contractor relationships, and leading a team of Technical Commercial specialists focused on delivering best-in-class commercial outcomes across major capital projects. Working closely with Engineering, Design, Delivery and Commercial teams, you will play a key role in securing critical mechanical equipment, services and supply chain capacity to support CDC's growing development pipeline.[](https://canberradc.sharepoint.com/sites/PeopleAndCulture/P%26C/_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7BB23C4EE4-C472-4D5B-8B81-1E0C6C94EBAC%7D&file=PD-502%20-%20Manager,%20Technical%20Commercial.docx&action=default&mobileredirect=true&DefaultItemOpen=1)

  • Lead and develop a small team responsible for the procurement and commercial management of mechanical equipment, materials and services.
  • Develop and execute procurement strategies that support project delivery, commercial outcomes and long-term operational requirements.
  • Support with tendering, supplier engagement, evaluation and contract negotiation activities.
  • Partner with engineering, design and project delivery teams to ensure procurement activities align with project schedules and technical requirements.
  • Build and manage strategic relationships with suppliers, manufacturers and contractors to secure supply chain capacity and drive performance.
  • Provide commercial leadership and recommendations on major procurement decisions, supplier selections and contract outcomes.
  • Identify and manage procurement, commercial and supply chain risks across key project packages.

What’s in it for you:

CDC offers excellent employment conditions and benefits such as:

  • CDC Academy - Make your mark by enhancing your professional development with the CDC Academy. Enrol in specialised training courses that will help you develop skills and ensure you thrive in your chosen career.
  • CDC Day - An additional day of paid leave dedicated to nurturing your health and wellbeing.
  • Parental Leave - Inclusive and above legislative tenure of parental leave entitlements to help you start, grow and care for your family.
  • Volunteer Leave - Make a meaningful difference with 2 days of volunteering leave for any cause or charity of your choice.
  • Employment Assistance Program - Be confident that you and your family are supported with access to our comprehensive Employee Assistance Program.
  • CDC Social Events - CDC’s offers staff and their family’s inclusive events that nurtures relationships, connection and friendships across the business. CDC hosts BBQs, family picnics and community events, bringing together CDC staff in different settings.

About You

You are a commercially minded procurement leader with experience delivering complex mechanical, building services, infrastructure or industrial projects. You combine strong technical understanding with commercial acumen and are confident managing supplier relationships, negotiating major contracts and influencing key stakeholders. You thrive in fast-paced project environments and enjoy working collaboratively to deliver practical, commercially sound outcomes.

  • Demonstrated experience in procurement, commercial management, strategic sourcing or supply chain leadership within mechanical services, construction, data centres or major capital projects.
  • Strong understanding of mechanical systems, equipment and contractor markets.
  • Demonstrated experience leading complex tendering, sourcing and contract negotiation activities.
  • The ability to build trusted relationships and influence technical, commercial and project stakeholders.
  • Experience managing high-value supplier and contractor relationships and driving performance outcomes.
  • Strong commercial, analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to balance cost, risk, quality and delivery requirements.
  • Previous leadership experience managing and developing procurement, commercial or project teams.

Essential:

Australian Citizenship with ability to obtain and maintain a NV1 Security Clearance.

How to Apply:

If you are looking for an opportunity to play a vital role in a fast-growing Australian Technology company and be part of our amazing team, please submit your resume and cover letter by clicking Apply.

We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace where all individuals are valued and respected. We believe that diversity of backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences leads to innovation and success. We actively promote equality and strive to create a welcoming environment for all employees. We are dedicated to building a team that reflects the diversity of our community and encourages everyone to bring their authentic selves to work.

job.title: Site Selection Director, Japan
job.description:
About Vantage

Vantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.

The Site Selection & Acquisitions (SSA) team is responsible for delivering quality sites for Vantage’s data center development. The team sources, evaluates, pre-qualifies, and completes initial due diligence leading to site acquisitions that support Vantage’s data center business across APAC. The team collaborates with Market Strategy, Sales, New Site Development, Design & Engineering, Construction, Operations, Legal, Finance and the Vantage Senior Leadership Team.

Ambitious growth of the core business has resulted in the Site Selection and Acquisitions team hiring top talent – internationally. Our headcount continues to increase, and this brings with it exciting opportunities for growth & learning. Join our team and your career will accelerate on the back of your exposure to the kind of responsibilities and variety that come with being part of an expanding business.

Position Overview

The successful candidate will be responsible for managing various data center site selection activities in line with Vantage’s strategic goals. Key elements of the role will include site selection for specific regions or markets, coordination with the Strategy and Market Intelligence team to deliver quality sites capable of supporting hyperscale data center campuses. This role is responsible for the acquisition strategy through pre-qualification, site due diligence, acquisition, closing and post-close management. Delivering sites in existing and future markets for Vantage that you would be given responsibility and support the larger SSA team to continue to expand across APAC will underpin all aspects of the role.

Essential Job Functions

  • Deliver quality sites in identified markets within key performance indicators regarding timing, project schedule, costs, risks, and technical requirements. This can be done through sourcing site through personal relationships, through third parties and from within the Vantage ecosystem/ relationships.
  • Lead all conversations and documentation for new site opportunities that are received through a bid process from third parties. Manage the interactions with Seller/ its agents, prepare expression of interest (EoI)/ letter of intent (LoI)/ presentation decks and work with internal teams to determine site’s suitability and price potential.
  • Prepare all internal documentation with regard to shortlisting a site as per standard internal Vantage process. Thes would be put together along with transaction managers of SSA and other relevant team members.
  • Lead all initial transaction closure related conversations such negotiating commercial terms, securing internal approval before those terms are finalised in an LoI or an equivalent document. Work closely with transaction managers of SSA who would support in taking the site acquisition to its complete closure.
  • Manage various aspects of site selection such as if all necessary use approvals have been secured by Seller, negotiations with landowners/ developers on non commercial terms such as easement, securing power approval/ infrastructure, support public policy team where community outreach is required and understand and ensure
  • implementation of necessary land transfer processes of local authorities having jurisdiction’s.
  • Coordinate local efforts with the various city planners, city councils, utilities and other relevant stakeholders that are critical to a project’s success in the various local markets.
  • - Represent Vantage in the best light to local officials and effectively communicate the benefits and value of wholesale data center campuses in their vicinity along with the public policy team
  • Work with Vice President, SSA, APAC to execute near term and multi-year strategic plans for the portfolio in conjunction with the Company’s Strategy. Work closely with VP, SSA, APAC to coordinate with Market Strategy, Sales, Corporate Development & other teams in preparation of this strategy, if required.
  • At the appropriate time, transition projects to the New Site Development team. Thereafter continue to work with legal & finance team to ensure site closure as per schedule and site handover completed as required.
  • Maintain responsibility for Seller/ developer engagement for all sites through the Design/Build/Operate cycles for activities related to Site Selection responsibilities.

Duties

  • Based on direction from internal stakeholders, deliver site selection options for new and existing markets within specified target areas on a regular basis.
  • Shortlist sites, negotiate best-in-class commercial terms for transactions and manage acquisition through closing and title registration.
  • Be the subject matter expert to the internal Vantage teams downstream of Site Selection on all site characteristics and transaction details.
  • Ensure all site data is stored, reported, and incorporated into Vantage plans-of-record.
  • Provide support to the New Site Development, Design & Engineering, Construction and Operations teams from concept through shovel ready state.
  • Coordinate with local real estate brokers/agents and consultants who will assist us in locating target properties.
  • Ensure lessons learned are held and placed in the feedback loop to drive continuous improvement.
  • Report status of all projects progressing through due diligence (risks, schedule, quality, and budget) to management.
  • Stay abreast of new technologies and opportunities to innovate build models and impact site selection methods, approaches, and criteria.
  • Coordinate with Finance, New Site Development/Design & Engineering/Construction Management Teams to establish project budgets and analyze design impacts on build costs and submit approval packages to the Executive Team.
  • Coordinate with local authorities, utilities, and government officials (with Executive support/approval).
  • Carry out preliminary evaluation of all new sites and new geographical markets in the current country of responsibility or any country identified for expansion. This includes the preliminary screening of all incoming new sites and opportunities, assuring all required documentation are gathered and analysis undertaken.
  • Assist in managing and expediting development activities and communicating entitlement and approval timelines.
  • Working with our internal Counsel and local counsel, oversee the drafting of all relevant acquisition documents within the acquisition life cycle, including Letters of Interest, Bid Documents, all forms of non-binding offers, Sale and Purchase Agreements, Asset Purchase Agreements, Share Purchase Vehicles, and related acquisition vehicles with the support of the Site Selection Manager and/or Transaction Manager.
  • Determine project feasibility, environmental review, due diligence, and risk assessment.
  • Effectively and constructively manage and coordinate the services of professional consultants such as planners, land use attorneys, energy development, and connectivity consultants, environmental, emissions, and others.

Job Requirements

  • Extensive experience in sourcing, negotiating, and acquiring large, complex sites with a high volume and velocity of deal flow in Japan.
  • A strong business network across the real estate sector (C-Suite access).
  • Minimum of +10 years’ experience in a real estate role for large, complex infrastructure projects.
  • Bachelor of Science degree in City Planning, Commercial Real Estate, Civil Engineering, Law, Surveying, or related field is preferred but not required.
  • Direct, hands-on experience in negotiating acquisitions and acquiring sites zoned for industrial, technical, or data center uses is a must.
  • Strong IT skills; ability to use multiple communication tools and packages
  • Tableau and Power BI skills preferred.
  • ArcGIS skills highly preferred.
  • Must possess excellent analytical skills with understanding of real estate finance, project IRR, and discounted cash flow analysis.
  • Ability to balance strategic thinking with tactical needs.
  • Ability to effectively respond to sensitive issues, complex inquiries, or complaints.
  • Ability to make effective presentations on general topics.
  • Skilled at solving problems and dealing with a variety of options with limited information.
  • Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram or schedule form.
  • Strong interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills at all levels of the organization and with other stakeholders and third parties such as suppliers.
  • Flexible, adaptable, team-player and self-directed; able to work in a variety of circumstances, e.g.: remotely, while travelling, across multiple time zones, cross functionally, by project, etc. This role would require travel domestically and internationally.

job.title: Senior Availability Management Analyst, APAC
job.description:
About Vantage

Vantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.

Regional Operations

The Regional Operations team plays a critical role in enabling safe, reliable, and scalable data center operations across the portfolio, ensuring consistent service delivery and operational performance for Vantage customers. Operating across multiple sites, the team provides the governance, systems, and operational frameworks required to maintain the health and integrity of infrastructure environments.

With deep expertise in mission critical operations, Regional Operations integrates engineering, service management, and operational support functions to drive consistency, performance, and continuous improvement. Responsibilities include establishing standardized operating practices for new and existing facilities, overseeing maintenance and capacity strategies, optimizing performance across sites, and ensuring effective response and recovery from unplanned events through coordinated regional support

About the Opportunity

Vantage's Critical Facility Operations teams manage our buildings and deliver best-in-class data centre services to our customers. At the front line are Critical Facility Engineers, responsible for the safe operation of critical electrical and mechanical infrastructure — work that demands deep operational knowledge and genuine fluency in service; change, incident and problem management. We are seeking a technically minded, organised and detail-oriented analyst to lead and govern the APAC Operations Service Management program across all three disciplines. The position is pivotal: it ensures every infrastructure change across our APAC data centres is executed with precision and transparency, and that every significant incident converts into a defensible root cause analysis and a corrective action that genuinely closes. You will be the regional focal point for governance, risk mitigation and compliance across our mission-critical environments.

You will own the change lifecycle end to end across all APAC sites — submission, approval, execution and post-change review — applying the Level of Risk (LOR) framework to classify changes and confirm that mitigation is proportionate and in place. The mandate extends equally to the post-event side: progressing the Problem lifecycle in ServiceNow, driving RCA (Root Cause Analysis) and Review completion against agreed service levels, holding the standard on record integrity across priority, Configuration Item and resolution coding, and maturing the APAC Known Error Database toward permanent engineered solutions. Success depends on close partnership with Site Operations, Engineering, Reliability and Customer teams, supported by training delivery, workflow optimisation and contribution to the APAC drill programme. You will also sustain audit readiness across change, incident and problem records, and produce the regional KPI and trend reporting on risk levels, RCA quality and corrective action closure that leadership relies on.

Your Duties and Responsibilities

  • Lead the implementation and continuous improvement of APAC Operations Change, Incident and Problem Management processes, ensuring alignment with global policies and operational excellence standards.
  • Oversee the end-to-end lifecycle of change requests and Problem records, from submission and initiation through approval, execution, root cause analysis and post-event review, across all APAC sites.
  • Ensure the Level of Risk (LOR) framework is applied, changes are appropriately categorised, incidents are correctly prioritised, and appropriate mitigation strategies are in place.
  • Act as the APAC authority on MOP, SOP and EOP standards, owning procedure quality, structure and governance across all sites. Lead training and coaching that builds site team capability, holds teams to a consistent standard and reduces operational risk.
  • Collaborate with Site Operations, Reliability Engineering and Customer teams to ensure clear communication and alignment on change, incident response and Problem investigation activities.
  • Maintain accurate records of all changes, incidents and Problems, ensuring documentation and record hygiene meet internal audit, customer and regulatory requirements.
  • Monitor Change, Incident and Problem metrics and KPIs to track approval timelines, risk levels, Root Cause Analysis (RCA) service level performance and corrective action closure.
  • Ensure RCA review outputs are reviewed for quality, completeness and evidence rigour, with corrective actions tracked through to validated closure.
  • Ensure documentation and related training materials are comprehensive, clear, and meet the needs of Operations teams, including incident response and Problem Management guidance.
  • Lead the APAC drill program as the regional authority on emergency readiness. Set drill standards, hold site teams accountable and lead training on escalation and EOP processes. Partner with the wider availability team on monthly performance reviews that turn findings into improvements in operational resilience.
  • Stay updated on industry best practices and emerging trends in data center Change, Incident and Problem Management, continuously seeking opportunities to enhance processes, tools and reporting capabilities used by the Operations Service Management teams.
  • Operate autonomously, making confident, independent decisions in high-pressure and time-critical situations. Stay firm and in control under pressure, take full ownership of outcomes and escalate only when needed.

Measures of Success

Success in this role will be demonstrated by:

  • No customer-impacting incident attributable to a change that was inadequately assessed, documented or routed
  • Draft and final RCA SLA compliance sustained across customer-facing and internal obligations
  • Sustained reduction in open, overdue and stale corrective actions on high impact problems
  • All high risk and emergency changes receive genuine independent review before authorisation
  • Change and problem record sets remain audit-ready without remediation effort
  • Documented improvement trend in process compliance across sites and vendors
  • Site teams and vendors demonstrably apply the process without escalation for routine work
  • Regional coverage maintained through rotation without dependence on the Manager for day-to-day decisions

Requirements

Ideally you will have these skills, qualifications, and characteristics:

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical or mechanical engineering, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of experience in critical facilities or data centre operations, with at least 2 years in a change management or governance role.
  • Strong understanding of mechanical and electrical infrastructure in mission-critical environments.
  • Familiarity with ITIL or similar change management frameworks.
  • Knowledge of data centre compliance standards (e.g., ISO, Uptime Institute)
  • Experience with ServiceNow or equivalent change management platforms.
  • Excellent communication, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Ability to work across time zones and cultures in a fast-paced, high-availability environment.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team, managing multiple priorities and deadlines.
  • Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to convey complex information clearly to various stakeholders.
  • Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and meet deadlines.
  • Attention to Detail and a High level of accuracy in written materials.
  • Able to adapt quickly, demonstrating a can-do attitude

You will thrive in this role if you bring a sharp eye for detail alongside a practical, outcome-focused mindset, and if you can uphold a high standard even when delivery pressure is on. It calls for confidence and conviction: schedules are tight and requesters move fast, so your value comes from being the person others trust to hold the line and get the documentation right. In return, you gain regional scope, direct visibility with VP-level stakeholders, and a clear pathway into broader service management.

We operate with No Ego and No Arrogance. We work to build each other up and support one another, appreciating each other’s strengths and respecting each other’s weaknesses. job.title: Manager, Facilities Operations, Taiwan
job.description:
About Vantage

Vantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.

#

Position Overview

The Manager, Facilities Operations will be responsible for continued and uninterrupted operation of raised floor 24-7-365 in a large Tier III data center campus to include all equipment and spaces up to the PDU at the customer level. The Manager will manage scheduled and corrective maintenance, system repairs, testing, equipment commissioning and all critical facility start up and continuing operations.

The Manager, Facilities Operations will manage and lead a team of Senior Level Specialists (Electrical and Mechanical) and Facility Technicians, as well as all contracted maintenance and repair teams working onsite in the facility. The Chief Engineer is responsible for the overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of these employees, and will report directly to the Director of Facilities Operations and coordinate activities with the Director of Engineering.

This position will be based on-site in one of our data center campuses.

Essential Job Functions

  • Oversee and supervise the efficient 24/7/365 operation of the facility equipment and systems.
  • Strive toward a goal of zero down-time in operations by virtue of reliable system performance.
  • Extensive customer service focus and interaction: evaluate all equipment and system operations, to include providing customers with engineering analysis, recommendations for improvement and energy efficiency methods.
  • Leadership and management of all assigned personnel, to include developing/conducting performance appraisals, training plans, counseling and mentoring.
  • Coordination, oversight and quality assurance supervision of maintenance and service repairs on all critical facility and building engineering systems to include (but not limited to); electrical distribution (12kv and lower), emergency diesel generators, UPS/Battery back-up systems, heating, ventilating and air conditioning systems (Chillers, CRACs, Cooling Towers, Package Units, etc.), BMS infrastructure, fire prevention as well as other electro-mechanical and control equipment throughout the data center campus.
  • Ensure all maintenance activities are performed in accordance with approved MOPs and the Vantage’s Mission Critical Facility work rules.
  • Utilizes the current CMMS program to administer and refine an effective preventative maintenance plan tailored to the facility.
  • Monitor and supervise subcontracted maintenance and repair projects, evaluating work performance and providing recommendations for utilizing in-house support whenever practical.
  • Ensure that work responsibilities are allocated properly among subordinates by developing and implementing manpower schedules and work methods and procedures that are designed to obtain low cost and efficient operation.
  • Establish performance standards for each phase of work, adhering to standard practices and quality levels.
  • Coordinate the development, implementation and training of SOP/EOP/MOPs for equipment and systems throughout the data center campus. This includes existing/supported equipment and systems as well as developing technical documentation for new and/or unsupported equipment and systems.
  • Run the site industrial safety program; assuring compliance with company policies, federal, state and local safety regulations.
  • Manage the site Lock-out / Tag-out program, strictly adhering to OSHA regulations.
  • Prepare operating and repair budgets, coordinating requirements with the Operations and Engineering Directors.
  • Oversee the purchasing of parts, equipment, and services to support operations within budget. Ensure adequate spare parts are maintained to allow expeditious repairs.
  • Establish and maintain periodic operational testing schedules for critical systems and equipment.
  • Conduct oversight of system testing and quality assurance documentation after major system repairs and/or maintenance to ensure compliance with EPA/environmental guidelines as well as local and state regulations.
  • Maintain and improve the site reliability program, identifying areas of concern that could develop into future problems.
  • Develop and maintain the site training program for technicians and other staff personnel on facility equipment and systems.
  • Perform other services determined necessary to maintain and operate all mission critical related infrastructure in an approved manner.
  • Additional duties as assigned by Management

Job Requirements

  • Minimum ten years of “hands on” maintenance/repair/installation/commissioning level experience in mission-critical facilities (mechanical and/or electrical), including experience with mission-critical infrastructure, or in a related industrial/engineering
  • At least two years of leadership/management experience - proven experience in project management, meeting deadlines, directing a maintenance department, and managing and developing staff in mission-critical infrastructure environments.
  • Possess complete understanding and working knowledge of 2N Data Center/Critical Facility infrastructure, systems, operations, maintenance and emergency responses.
  • Strong Technical Writing skills and experience; as well as creating, coordinating, updating and/or modifying MOP/EOP/SOPs for critical facilities equipment, to include supporting new systems and researching technical requirements.
  • Excellent customer service experience with the ability and desire to engage customers at the site to explain infrastructure or engineering related concepts, methods of improvement or explaining emergency procedures.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to maintain constant interaction with supervisors and managers, as well as technicians in order to maintain awareness of critical facility activities.
  • Experience developing budgets, future plans, capital investments and repair projects with management and coordinating financial requests up to the CEO level as well as training subordinates to remain within budget.
  • Must be open to long hours, weekend, rotating shifts, and subject to calls during hours away from plant (24/7).
  • Potential managers must successfully complete a background check and drug screen.
  • Travel is expected to be minimal, up to 5% for training.

job.description:

With a rapidly expanding footprint across APAC, STACK combines deep development expertise, flexible capital, and operational discipline to deliver critical digital infrastructure at scale.

job.title: Lead - Security Operations
job.description:
Security Strategy Implementation:

Collaborate with the CSO and Head - Security to develop, refine, and implement security strategies, policies, and frameworks in line with evolving industry standards and airport security needs.

Provide insights and data from operational activities to help shape long-term security plans and initiatives.

Lead initiatives for continuous improvement, ensuring that security systems evolve with the changing threat landscape and as per the regulation. Drive the adoption of new technologies and best practices across airports.

Operational Management: ( landside / AVSEC / Loss Prevention):

Oversee security operations across airports, ensuring that security measures are implemented across all airport sites effectively and consistently.

Ensure that effective incident response mechanisms are in place at each airport. Provide guidance and support during major security incidents or emergencies.

Regularly monitor and assess the performance of security teams at different airports, ensuring they meet performance targets and compliance standards.

Oversee security audits, both internal and external, and ensure that airports meet all regulatory compliance requirements. Address any audit findings and implement corrective actions.

Risk Assessment and Security Intelligence:

Regularly conduct security risk assessments for the network of airports. Identify emerging threats and risks, and develop strategies for mitigation.

Work closely with local, national, and international intelligence agencies to gather security-related information. Ensure the proactive management of potential security threats based on this information.

Monitor and analyze global and regional security trends to adjust security strategies accordingly. Ensure that vigilance levels are maintained high across all airport sites.

Policy Development & Compliance:

Assist CSO and Head security in Design, implement, and review security policies, procedures, and programs to safeguard people, assets, and infrastructure, ensuring compliance with local and international regulations.

Drive the implementation of AVSEC standards per ICAO Annex 17, NCASP, NCASQ BCAS, and other governing bodies, and ensure compliance with the latest aviation security practices.

Strive to continuously improve the design, operation, implementation and maintenance of ASP, AVSEC standards as established by BCAS and other regulatory authority.

Crisis & Incident Management:

Oversee and Develop, implement, and periodically update crisis management plans for all airports. Lead the response during major security breaches, emergencies, or incidents.

Ensure that crisis management training and simulations are conducted regularly across all airports. Guide Head - Security to prepare teams for a variety of emergency scenarios, ensuring readiness at all times.

Oversee recovery processes to ensure the swift restoration of normal operations following any security incidents. Develop and ensure business continuity protocols are in place across the network.

Stakeholder Engagement and Communication:

Serve as the primary liaison between security teams at different airports and other key stakeholders, including law enforcement agencies, airport management, and regulatory bodies.

Build and maintain strong relationships with regulatory bodies such as BCAS, DGCA, ICAO, and local law enforcement to ensure compliance with security regulations.

Provide regular updates to senior management and relevant stakeholders on the status of security operations, ongoing challenges, and potential risks.

Budgeting and Resource Management:

Oversee the security budget for the entire network of airports. Ensure cost-effective allocation of resources for security systems, staffing, and training.

Ensure that sufficient resources, including personnel, technology, and equipment, are available to meet operational needs at all airports.

Ensure that financial expenditures related to security operations are in line with approved budgets. Assist in the procurement process for security equipment and systems.

Security Technology & Automation Support:

Oversee the integration of advanced security technologies (CCTV, access control, surveillance systems, Screening systems etc.) across all airports. Ensure that security systems are regularly maintained and upgraded.

Champion the adoption of cutting-edge security solutions to enhance operational efficiency and response times. Drive the use of data analytics and AI for security operations where applicable.

Team Leadership and Development:

Lead, mentor, and support the security leadership team, including Head - Security at each airport. Provide guidance on handling complex security issues and promoting a culture of continuous improvement.

Ensure ongoing professional development and training programs for security staff at all levels. Promote a culture of excellence in security practices.

Establish clear performance goals, conduct regular evaluations, and provide constructive feedback to security teams across all airports.

Key Stakeholders - Internal:

CSO

Head - Security

Operations Team

Facilities Team

Compliance Department

IT and ISOC teams

Key Stakeholders - External:

Regulatory Authorities

Airport Officials

CISF

Outsourced Security Vendors

Passengers and Visitors

Security Contractors or Third-Party Providers

Qualifications

Education Qualification:

Bachelor’s degree in preferably in Security Management, Aviation Security, Criminal Justice, or a related field.

Certifications in security and crisis management, such as Certified Protection Professional (CPP), Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), Certified Fraud Examiner ( CFE)

Work Experience:

15-20 years of experience ( Depending on the site complexity/ requirement) in security operations or preferably with experience in airport security management.

In-depth knowledge of security processes and standards. Aviation security regulations, standards, and best practices, security technologies, risk assessment methodologies, and threat analysis

job.title: Senior Engineer - Cell Process
job.description:
About Business:

Adani Group: Adani Group is a diversified organisation in India comprising 10 publicly traded companies. It has created a world class logistics and utility infrastructure portfolio that has a pan-India presence. Adani Group is headquartered in Ahmedabad, in the state of Gujarat, India. Over the years, Adani Group has positioned itself to be the market leader in its logistics and energy businesses focusing on large scale infrastructure development in India with O & M practices benchmarked to global standards. With four IG rated businesses, it is the only Infrastructure Investment Grade issuer in India.

Adani Solar: Adani Solar is India's 1st and largest vertically integrated solar PV manufacturer with 4 GW cells & modules and 2 GW of ingots & wafers manufacturing capacities

Job Purpose: The job purpose of a Shift Engineer - Cluster - Diffusion in solar manufacturing is to oversee and optimize the diffusion process crucial for doping silicon wafers in solar cell production. This role ensures efficient operation, uniform doping for desired electrical properties, work on completion of already defined DOEs and report compilation of Junction depth, junction conc. and adherence to quality and safety standards, contributing to the production of high-performance solar cells.

Responsibilities

Safety and Compliance :

  • Ensure adherence to safety protocols and regulatory standards, conducting regular audits and training to maintain a safe work environment. Proactively identify risks and implement corrective actions to ensure full compliance with safety regulations.

Optimization of Process Recipe:

  • Continuously optimize process recipes for Wet-Line, Diffusion, Pre & Post Oxidation, Laser, PECVD, and Backend processes to improve efficiency and quality.

Process Optimization:

  • Optimize diffusion parameters to maximize efficiency and yield of solar cells, continually improving processes to enhance performance and reliability.

Equipment Management:

  • Manage diffusion furnaces and related equipment, ensuring proper operation, calibration, and maintenance to minimize downtime and ensure reliability.

Quality Control:

  • Conduct rigorous inspections and quality checks to maintain uniform doping and meet product specifications, implementing corrective actions as needed to uphold high-quality standards.

Troubleshooting and Problem Solving:

  • Identify and resolve technical issues during the diffusion process, employing root cause analysis and proactive measures to minimize disruptions and improve process stability.

Documentation and Reporting:

  • Maintain accurate records of process parameters, production data, and quality metrics, generating reports to track performance indicators and support continuous improvement efforts.

Key Stakeholders - Internal:

  • Cluster Manager - Cell Process
  • Technicians and Operators within Cell Process
  • Quality Control Inspectors

Key Stakeholders - External:

  • Equipment Suppliers
  • Maintenance Contractors
  • Regulatory Authorities

Qualifications

Educational Qualification:

  • B.Tech – Electronics/Chemical / Metallurgy/ Renewable Energy
  • Desired Qualification : BE/B.Tech

Work Experience (Range of years):

  • Min 2 - 5 years of experience in diffusion process management, including cycle time reduction, yield enhancement, and process parameter optimization.

Certification:

job.title: Executive - Billing & MIS
job.description:
Billing and Invoice Verification:

Ensure the accurate measurement and verification of completed work for all services rendered, ensuring that the quantity and quality of work align with agreed terms.

Process and upload verified invoices into the billing systems, such as SAP or ARIBA, while ensuring all transactions comply with the terms and conditions outlined in service agreements and contracts.

MIS Reporting and Data Maintenance:

Generate and maintain comprehensive reports detailing operational performance, maintenance activities, and the status of services, ensuring the data is accurate and up-to-date.

Ensure that all reports are submitted to relevant stakeholders within the specified deadlines, adhering to established timelines and communication protocols for smooth information flow.

Vendor Management Support:

Assist in the creation and ongoing maintenance of vendor records for services, ensuring all relevant information is accurately captured and updated in the vendor management system.

Monitor and ensure that the services delivered by vendors consistently meet the agreed contractual obligations, supporting effective management and oversight of vendor relationships.

Work Order Management:

Support the creation, tracking, and closure of work orders for ongoing maintenance and service activities, ensuring all necessary information is recorded and accessible for future reference.

Ensure that work orders are processed efficiently in line with operational requirements and are closed promptly once all maintenance tasks have been completed and verified as satisfactory.

Service and Asset Documentation:

Maintain accurate and detailed records of all maintenance and servicing activities performed on equipment and assets, ensuring documentation is thorough and easily accessible for future audits and reporting.

Ensure that all service reports, completion certificates, and asset condition assessments are accurately documented, reviewed, and stored for future reference and regulatory compliance.

Monitor Budget Allocations and Expenditures:

Track and analyze budget utilization across projects or departments to ensure adherence to allocated funds.

Prepare periodic financial summaries and variance reports to highlight deviations and recommend corrective actions.

Compliance Monitoring for Operational Activities:

Ensure that all maintenance and operational activities comply with established health, safety, and environmental standards, regularly reviewing procedures to identify areas of improvement.

Assist in conducting internal audits of maintenance processes, ensuring that all activities meet regulatory requirements and supporting compliance with industry standards for service delivery.

job.title: Lead - Dcs/plc - C&I
job.description:
Lead - DCS_PLC (Distributed Control System_ Programmable Logic Control)

System Reliability and Maintenance:

Ensure the availability and functioning of all control loops in auto mode, maintaining reliability of equipment protection under BTG.

Schedule and execute regular backups of DCS and PLC systems to prevent data loss.

Perform routine maintenance and troubleshooting of DCS and PLC hardware to minimize downtime.

Monitor system alarms daily and ensure the healthiness and redundancy of systems.

Coordinate with Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) for annual maintenance activities and system upgrades.

Manage the proper functioning of Operator Workstations (OWS) and Engineering Workstations (EWS).

Maintain periodical backups and availability of historian systems for data integrity and recovery.

Hardware and Software Management:

Manage the availability of DCS and PLC hardware and software, including necessary spares for emergency replacements.

Maintain up-to-date DCS and PLC licenses and manage renewals to avoid operational disruptions.

Conduct patch updates of DCS and PLC software to address vulnerabilities and enhance system performance.

Upgrade DCS and PLC systems proactively to prevent obsolescence and maintain compatibility with new technologies.

Network and Cybersecurity:

Manage the storage, backup, and restoration of systems in compliance with cybersecurity policies.

Ensure the healthiness and redundancy of the DCS and PLC network, preventing single points of failure.

Oversee the transfer of data to third-party systems, such as Pi servers, ensuring secure and reliable communication.

Review and strengthen network security measures to protect against cyber threats and unauthorized access.

Business Sustainability:

Implement and Follow IMS, AWMS, DISHA and CHETNA guidelines within the department.

Promote the safety of personnel and equipment through rigorous training and strict adherence to safety protocols.

Implement risk management practices to mitigate potential hazards and ensure operational continuity.

Develop and maintain emergency response plans to address potential incidents swiftly and effectively.

Ensure adherence to statutory compliances and regulations.

Implement MoC (Management of Change) protocols to ensure safe and compliant modifications to equipment and processes.

Provide support for Root Cause Analysis (RCA), Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), Zero Forced Outage (ZFO) to enhance system reliability.

Implement field related ZFO action items and AWMS for continuous improvement in maintenance practices.

.

Digitization and Automation:

Execute comprehensive digitization strategies and automation solutions to optimize operational efficiency.

Implement process and system improvements, adopting newer technologies and innovative ideas.

Drive the implementation of digital transformation initiatives.

Analyse data trends and system performance to identify opportunities for automation and digitization enhancements.

Environment & Sustainability

Techno Commercial

Operations & Maintenance

Security

Stores

Support Functions

ENDORSE

ENOC

Key Stakeholders - External:

Vendor

Bachelor's degree in C&I or Electronics & Communication or equivalent degree.

Work Experience (Range of years):

8+ years of experience in industrial automation, specifically with DCS and PLC systems.

Preferred Industry:

Experience in the power generation, petrochemical, oil and gas, or heavy industrial sectors.

job.title: Electrical & MIS Lead (PSP Hydro - O&M)
job.description:
Responsibilities

  • Ensure reliable, safe and efficient operation of all generating units, auxiliaries, and balance of plant systems.
  • Ensures full compliance with Statutory HSS, environmental and technical requirements from central and state governmental bodies (i.e. CEA, CERC, DSA, SCEI, AP/CPCB etc. compliances).
  • Developing safe systems of work (SSOW) procedures, including HIRA, PTW, LOTO, JSA etc. for your area.
  • To provide oversight of all electrical maintenance activities, management of the maintenance teams, financial control, contract management, environmental compliance, regulatory compliance, technical compliance, risk evaluations and relationship management.
  • Ensure O&M for electrical systems at Hydro and PSP Assets are aligned and carried out in line to prevailing O&M practices in the organization.
  • Implement analytical tools, procedures, protocols etc. for ensuring efficient and effective monitoring, cost and performance optimization of Electrical systems/works at Hydro and PSP Assets.
  • Prepare maintenance strategy to achieve higher reliability (maximized MTTF) and greater efficiency (minimized MTTR) and implement the maintenance plans at plant level accordingly.
  • Lead equipment failure investigations and analysis, establish RCA framework and implement performance monitoring, corrective actions and continuous improvement methodology, for your area.
  • Preparation of service contract and contract management for electrical maintenance works outsourced to external service providers.
  • Guide and support electrical section head for preparation and implementation of complete plant maintenance reports and checklists, including daily, monthly, quarterly, and annual reports and checklists.
  • Plans and leads major upgradations at Hydro and PSP assets for Electrical systems.
  • Establishment of Computerized Maintenance Management Systems (CMMS) at plant level, taking lead for electrical systems.
  • Guides and supports Hydro and PSP electrical section heads in preparation of maintenance budget, work to optimize the costs and maximize production. This includes developing and tracking the monthly, quarterly, and annual maintenance budgets.
  • Define and monitor maintenance plans to achieve yearly Generation targets (including minimization of APC consumption) and yearly agreed Plant/Machines Availability targets.
  • Support Hydro and PSP electrical section heads in plant improvement projects, modernization initiatives, digital transformation, and automation upgrades.
  • Maintains plant critical spares inventory, in coordination with section heads, to meet the exigencies.
  • Train and develop electrical maintenance team at Plant and prepare a detailed training calendar for electrical maintenance team accordingly.
  • Develop and execute risk management strategies to mitigate maintenance related risks and ensure compliance with internal audits.
  • Guide and support Hydro and PSP electrical section heads in developing electrical maintenance records and present the same to management on need basis.
  • Support Hydro and PSP Assets for IMS implementation, documentation preparation and updating, pertaining to your area (i.e., Electrical systems).
  • Provide support to Hydro and PSP electrical section heads in ensuring the production equipment are in good working condition, are reliable for use, and are maintained at an optimal cost.
  • Ensures electrical maintenance activities are performed in a safe, professional manner and in accordance with the industry standards, original equipment manufacturer’s recommendations and in line to approved standard operating procedures.
  • Proffer solutions to solve electrical system related issues faced at Assets and ensure optimization of equipment reliability.
  • Coordinate and monitor implementation of reliability centred maintenance (RCM) in conjunction with relevant section heads at Hydro and PSP Assets.
  • Ensures compliance with industry standards, regulations, safety protocols, and safe system to work (SSOW) procedures.
  • Staying up to date with the latest trends, innovations, and best practices in electrical engineering, to drive continuous improvement.
  • Ensure that all electrical aspects of the operations are managed effectively and efficiently.

Qualifications

  • B.E/B. Tech/M.Tech in Electrical Engineering.
  • 15+ years of experience in O&M in large scale hydropower plants.
  • Strong knowledge of Statutory and regulatory requirements pertaining to Hydro and PSS Plants.
  • Maintenance experience of large-scale hydro and/or pump storage power plants is preferred
  • Experience with CMMS (Computerized Maintenance Management Systems) for Plant maintenance works.
  • Knowledge of analytics tools for performance optimization and risk assessment.
  • Advanced certifications in maintenance management or other power generation technologies or energy manager and auditor certification are preferred

Develop greenhouse gas (GHG), carbon offset, and biodiversity replenishment programs, that are relevant to the data center industry, that align with our stated ESG goals

  • Community engagement and impact
  • STEM and education initiatives
  • Environmental volunteering
  • Inclusion and industry access

Ensure localisation of programmes while maintaining global alignment and brand consistency. Work with legal and compliance teams to vet our CSR partners

Employee engagement and team building

  • Personal development
  • Culture and values activation

Develop toolkits and guidance for managers to drive participation at scale across all locations.

External Education, Social Impact and Partnerships

  • Build and manage strategic partnerships with NGOs, educational institutions, community organisations and industry bodies
  • Identify and scale initiatives that strengthen the company’s social licence to operate in local markets.
  • Drive programmes aligned to workforce strategy (e.g. STEM pipelines, community talent development) including but not limited to Educational Institution relationships and curriculum building, employee guest lecturing and industry awareness initiatives
  • Represent the company in CSR-related forums and partnerships as delegated by the Head of ESG.

**

  • Establish and maintain CSR metrics, dashboards, and reporting frameworks aligned to ESG reporting
  • Track programme effectiveness including participation rates, social impact outcomes, and brand impact.

Annual sustainability reports

Ensure strong governance and consistency across markets.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Corporate Communications on storytelling and brand amplification

  • Country leadership on local execution
  • Commercial and customer teams where CSR supports customer engagement or RFP positioning

Act as the central coordination point for CSR activity across the organisation.

Culture, Capability and Internal Awareness

Campaigns and communications

  • Leadership engagement
  • Employee storytelling

Embed CSR as a visible and tangible part of the company’s purpose and values. Support a culture of community contribution, inclusivity and responsible business practices

The successful candidate:

  • Proven track record in executing multi-country CSR or employee engagement programmes.
  • Experience working in complex, matrixed organisations across Asia or globally.
  • Strong partnership experience with HR, Communications and external stakeholders.
  • Experience in sectors such as infrastructure, technology, data centres or industrial environments preferred

Key Attributes

  • Strong stakeholder management and influencing capability across all levels.
  • Commercially aware, with the ability to align CSR outcomes to business priorities.
  • Highly collaborative, culturally aware and adaptable across markets.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to connect purpose, people and impact.

**

Join us to shape the future of Digital Infrastructure in Asia. Apply now for a confidential career discussion.

  • Provide egional Health and Safety input into project development and transition from design through construction, commissioning, and operations, ensuring key risks and controls are understood and effectively managed.
  • Oversee Health and Safety risk management across construction and operational activities operating concurrently within the same perimeter, ensuring safe segregation, interface management, and coordination between construction and operations teams over multi-year build-out programs.
  • Provide regional Health and Safety input into project handover from design to construction, ensuring key risks and controls identified during design are understood and managed on site.
  • Directly manage Country Leads / Managers of Health and Safety, providing direction, coaching, and performance oversight to strengthen capability and accountability across the region.
  • Build a strong regional Health and Safety team through talent development, training, and succession planning across country-level leadership
  • Drive consistent implementation of corporate Health and Safety systems, standards, and procedures across all covered markets.
  • Monitor regional Health and Safety performance, trends, and leading indicators to identify systemic risks and drive accountability at country level, and communicate key risks and improvement priorities to regional and country leadership.
  • Review significant Health and Safety incidents and high-potential events across the region, ensuring robust investigations, root cause analysis, corrective actions, and cross-country application of lessons learned..
  • Provide Health and Safety input into contractor and vendor prequalification, selection, performance reviews, and ongoing assurance activities across the region.
  • Engage with regional Construction and Operations leadership to manage high-risk activities, emerging risks, and significant Health and Safety issues.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable Health and Safety and environmental regulatory requirements, including oversight of ISO 45001 and ISO 14001 management system conformance across covered markets..
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives and strengthen Health and Safety culture, capability, and accountability across the region.
  • Support Health and Safety inputs for customer requirements, lender engagements, and external stakeholder reporting where required.
  • Actively champion and implement the organization’s policies on health and safety, environment, energy, quality, information security, and business continuity, ensuring adherence to incident reporting, legal, and regulatory requirements.

**

The successful candidate:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Occupational Health and Safety, Engineering, Environmental Science, or a related discipline, with recognized professional Health and Safety qualifications or certifications.
  • 15+ years of progressive Health and Safety experience, including significant regional leadership experience across large-scale construction and/or operational environments.
  • Proven experience in Health and Safety leadership and risk management within large-scale, complex, mission-critical or high-risk environments, including data centers, pharmaceutical, chemical, or process industries.
  • Proven experience directly managing and developing Health and Safety teams across multiple sites or countries, including performance management, coaching, and capability building of direct reports.
  • Strong track record influencing senior regional leadership, Construction and Operations teams, contractors, and other stakeholders to achieve measurable Health and Safety performance improvements.
  • Strong knowledge of international Health and Safety standards, risk management principles, and experience navigating regulatory requirements across multiple Asian markets.
  • Demonstrated ability to provide Health and Safety leadership across construction, commissioning, and live operational environments, with regular travel across the region.
  • Fluent in English; additional Hindi / Thai / Indonesian / Malay language capability is an advantage.

job.title: Operations Manager
job.description:
Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia

Company

Singtel Group

Be a part of something BIG!

Say HELLO to BIG Possibilities with Singtel KL (Sudong MY Sdn Bhd)!

Singtel is Asia's leading communications technology group, our presence spans across 21 countries in Asia, Australia, and Africa. We thrive on innovation, digital transformation, and harnessing next-generation technology to create a more sustainable and digital future. Now, we are bringing this energy to Kuala Lumpur with the launch of our brand-new Shared Services Centre.

We are looking for an Operations Manager to lead and oversee Managed Services operations, ensuring seamless service delivery, operational excellence and compliance with agreed service levels. This role will drive operational governance, cross-functional collaboration and continuous improvement, with a key focus on managing the 24x7 Service Delivery Centre (SDC) to ensure service reliability, timely incident resolution and effective resource utilisation.

**

Make an Impact by

**

  • Provide overall operational leadership, governance and oversight across multiple support teams, ensuring service delivery meets agreed SLAs, operational standards and cost targets.
  • Lead and oversee 24x7 Service Delivery Centre (SDC) operations, ensuring continuous monitoring, timely incident response, effective escalation and operational continuity.
  • Ensure incidents, alerts and service disruptions are promptly identified, prioritised, investigated and escalated to the appropriate technical resolver teams.
  • Drive operational accountability across teams, ensuring clear ownership of incidents, service requests, operational risks and customer-impacting issues.
  • Manage workforce planning, shift scheduling, manpower allocation and contingency arrangements to maintain uninterrupted 24x7 operational coverage.
  • Oversee local people and administrative matters, including onboarding, employee coordination, performance management support and workforce requirements.
  • Monitor operational KPIs, including SLA compliance, incident restoration, alert response, service availability, operational backlog, change success rates and cost efficiency.
  • Act as the key coordination point between Sudong and ES HQ, ensuring alignment of operational priorities, dependencies and service commitments.
  • Collaborate with functional leaders, technical teams, vendors and stakeholders to resolve operational challenges, manage escalations and drive service improvements.
  • Oversee User Access Management (UAM) activities, ensuring timely access provisioning, modifications, revocations and periodic reviews in compliance with governance requirements.
  • Monitor scheduled patching, maintenance and operational activities, ensuring timely completion and escalation of unsuccessful or outstanding tasks.
  • Govern NOC and Telco Change Request operations, ensuring compliance with approved change procedures, implementation plans, rollback processes and operational readiness requirements.
  • Maintain and enhance operational SOPs, runbooks, escalation procedures and shift handover processes to ensure consistency, accuracy and service continuity.
  • Identify recurring incidents, operational inefficiencies and service gaps, implementing corrective, preventive and automation initiatives to improve operational performance.
  • Conduct regular operational performance reviews and provide management reporting on service health, risks, resource capacity, productivity and improvement initiatives.
  • Drive continuous improvement, operational transformation and process standardisation to enhance service reliability, operational efficiency and customer satisfaction.

**

**

Skills for Success

  • Degree or equivalent professional qualification in Engineering, Information Technology, Telecommunications, Business Management, Operations Management or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 10 years of experience in telecommunications, IT services, Managed Services, service delivery or operational management.
  • Proven experience leading large-scale or multi-functional operational teams within a complex service delivery environment.
  • Strong experience in operational governance, service assurance, incident management, escalation management and SLA performance monitoring.
  • Experience managing or supporting 24x7 operations, including workforce planning, shift management and operational continuity, is highly preferred.
  • Sound knowledge of ITIL frameworks, IT service management practices and operational service delivery processes.
  • Strong capabilities in manpower planning, capacity management, resource optimisation, performance management and cost control.
  • Good understanding of NOC operations, change management, User Access Management, patching and maintenance activities.
  • Excellent leadership, stakeholder management, communication and cross-functional coordination skills.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving and decision-making abilities, with the capability to manage critical incidents and operational risks effectively.
  • Experience working with geographically distributed teams, offshore operations or captive shared services environments will be an advantage.
  • Exposure to operational transitions, service transformation, process improvement or automation initiatives will be beneficial.

Be a Part of Something BIG!

**

Support the Group CTO Office in driving network cost leadership, technology investment optimization and programme oversight across Singtel Group, OpCos and Regional Associates. The role provides technical and commercial support for network RFPs and investments, drives regional benchmarking and cost optimization, program management, and facilitates regional collaboration to achieve measurable Group synergies and business outcomes.

Make an impact by

**

Network Cost Management & Commercial Benchmarking

  • Leverage Group scale and synergies to achieve competitive cost positions and sustainable network cost leadership across Singtel Group, OpCos and Associates.

  • Maintain the GTN portfolio on strategic programmes and GTN work plans across OpCo and Associates, track and consolidate programme status for GCTO reporting.
